focus: Overlap load and compute with ping-pong buffers or a canonical dataflow schedule.
merge_rule: Union of gemm_flatten_v1 and flash_no_RMW overlay. On id conflicts, the no-RMW overlay replaces the v1 entry.

skills.pattern: load-compute-store tiling where DATAFLOW overlap between stages is desired and tile dependencies permit concurrent stages
skills.strategy: Factor each tile into a helper function whose body is a canonical DATAFLOW region containing only buffer/stream declarations plus exactly three calls: load function, compute function, store function.
required_steps: define load_tile, compute_tile, store_tile as separate synthesizable functions
helper process_tile_lcs contains #pragma HLS DATAFLOW with declarations + three calls only
outer host loop uses unit tile index; compute tile_i = tile * TILE_SIZE before calling helper
no if/else, dynamic tile calculations, or non-unit increments inside the DATAFLOW region
verify overlap report: concurrent stages, not merely alternating buffer names
guards: use hls::stream or ping-pong locals only when fifo depth covers stage latency
skip DATAFLOW entirely if stages cannot overlap — use pipelined sequential phases

skills.pattern: multiple compute tasks under #pragma HLS DATAFLOW each read the same local array (matrix reused in two GEMMs, dual matvec on same A, or stat pipeline mean→stddev→normalize all touching local_data) — HLS 200-779
skills.strategy: Merge every compute phase that shares a local input or intermediate into ONE static compute_fused_task with sequential labeled loops inside. Keep parallel load_* and store_* as separate DATAFLOW tasks. Never add an inline for-loop copy inside DATAFLOW to dodge fan-out — that creates another reader process.
required_steps: list compute tasks and mark which locals each reads/writes
if two+ compute tasks read the same local (e.g. local_A, local_data_in, local_tmp): fold into one compute_fused_task
if one intermediate is consumed by downstream compute AND store_tmp: either store inside the fused compute after last use, or chain linearly compute_fused → local_out read only by store
for chained GEMMs (tmp = alpha*A*B; D = beta*D + tmp*C): one task does both nests sequentially; parallel loads for A,B,C,D_in; parallel stores for tmp and D_out only after fused compute completes
for dual matvec (tmp=A*x; y=A'*tmp): one task reads local_A once for both phases
for stat pipelines (mean, stddev, normalize, corr): one compute_stats_task with sequential loops; parallel store_mean/store_stddev/store_corr OK after
guards: fused compute task must not take m_axi port pointers
do not place copy loops inside DATAFLOW region — use separate copy task or fuse into compute
preserve numerical order when merging phases

skills.pattern: two compute tasks under #pragma HLS DATAFLOW both read the same local array produced by an upstream task (e.g. compute_x and compute_w both consume local_A_out) — HLS 200-779
skills.strategy: Merge the parallel consumer compute tasks into one compute_xw_task with sequential labeled loops, or insert hls::stream between producer and a single downstream consumer. Never leave two concurrent reader tasks on the same local buffer.
required_steps: identify locals with one writer and two+ reader compute tasks
merge consumers into one static task with both computation nests inside
if merge hurts II, use hls::stream from producer to one consumer and duplicate producer output via second stream (tee) — never two tasks reading same local
tile loops wrapping DATAFLOW: each tile iteration must use private tile buffers; still no fan-out within one DATAFLOW invocation
guards: merged task stays locals-only — no m_axi pointers
store tasks may run parallel only if each reads a distinct local output

skills.pattern: one local array written by a compute task and read by two or more concurrent DATAFLOW tasks (e.g. compute stage + store stage + downstream compute all touch local_tmp)
skills.strategy: Every local array in a DATAFLOW region must have exactly one writer task and exactly one reader task. For fan-out (one producer, multiple consumers), chain with hls::stream FIFOs, duplicate into separate single-use buffers (buf_for_compute / buf_for_store), or merge consumers into one task.
required_steps: list every local array and mark writer task + reader task
reject any local with >1 writer or >1 concurrent reader
if compute writes local_M and both store and a later compute read local_M, insert hls::stream between producer and each consumer OR serialize store after final consumer in a linear chain
for load→compute handoff use buf_in written only by load, read only by compute; compute writes buf_out read only by store
re-run csynth until HLS 200-779 / 200-979 are gone
guards: ping-pong buf0/buf1 still obeys one writer per bank per time step
hls::stream depth ≥ 2 when producer may run ahead of consumer
do not pass the same local array into three task calls under one #pragma HLS DATAFLOW

skills.pattern: DATAFLOW structure passes csynth but latency is high because compute tasks lack ARRAY_PARTITION, inner UNROLL, and parallel load/store overlap
skills.strategy: After correct DATAFLOW task boundaries, maximize throughput: partition local arrays on the inner compute dimension, UNROLL inner loops to match partition factor, pipeline innermost loops II=1, run independent load tasks in parallel on distinct gmemN bundles, and use hls::stream depth 4–16 for tile pipelines to overlap load(t+1) with compute(t).
required_steps: add #pragma HLS ARRAY_PARTITION cyclic or block on hot local arrays — factor matches UNROLL
add #pragma HLS UNROLL factor=UF on innermost reduction/dot-product loop
pipeline innermost memory/compute loop with II=1; never outer row loop PIPELINE for multi-matrix loads
issue parallel load tasks only when each touches a different m_axi port/bundle
for tiled kernels use hls::stream tile FIFO between load_tile, compute_tile, store_tile for real overlap
target higher DSP/FF utilization when latency slack exists — prefer parallelism over minimal resources
guards: partition/unroll must not break DATAFLOW buffer ownership rules
BRAM budget: tile smaller or stream panels instead of full-matrix locals
complements hls-array-partition-match-unroll-factor from base skills

skills.pattern: kernel uses or proposes #pragma HLS DATAFLOW, ping-pong buffers, or double-buffered tile staging
skills.strategy: Do not add ping-pong buffers or DATAFLOW unless the code expresses a valid canonical producer-consumer schedule with real overlap. Default to single local buffer + pipelined load/compute/store loops when true cross-tile overlap is not implemented.
required_steps: audit every DATAFLOW region: only declarations and function calls — no if/else, dynamic tile math, or non-unit increments inside
use unit-increment tile index: for (tile=0; tile<NUM_TILES; tile++) with tile_i = tile * TILE_SIZE — never DATAFLOW inside tile_i += TILE_SIZE
reject ping-pong that only alternates buffers across sequential tile iterations without load(t+1) overlapping compute/store(t)
for triangular factorization/solve or other cross-tile dependencies, prove tile overlap is legal before ping-pong or DATAFLOW across tiles
factor load-compute-store DATAFLOW into a helper with load_fn(); compute_fn(); store_fn(); calls only
if no true overlap, use one local buffer and fix loop II, memory access, and reductions first
report whether ping-pong provides actual overlap; if not, remove ping-pong and DATAFLOW
guards: decorative DATAFLOW/ping-pong wastes BRAM and can block II fixes
fifo/stream depths must match real producer-consumer latency when overlap exists
sequential tile processing with cross-tile deps forbids fake overlap
skills.template:
OVERLAP REPORT (required if ping-pong/DATAFLOW present):
| stage pairing | overlap? | evidence |

BAD: sequential tiles with buf[tile&1] but no concurrent load/compute
GOOD: #pragma HLS DATAFLOW + load_tile(t+1) || compute_tile(t) with proven independence

skills.pattern: kernel has two or more m_axi pointer ports and uses #pragma HLS DATAFLOW or multiple load/compute/store tasks that should overlap external memory access
skills.strategy: Assign a distinct bundle=gmem0, gmem1, … to each m_axi pointer port so HLS can issue concurrent external memory transactions across DATAFLOW stages. Never place all read/write ports on a single bundle=gmem when stages are meant to run concurrently.
required_steps: enumerate every m_axi port on the top kernel and on DATAFLOW subfunctions that touch global memory
assign each pointer port a unique bundle=gmemN (gmem0, gmem1, gmem2, …)
map load tasks to read ports and store tasks to write ports on separate bundles when stages overlap
re-run csynth and verify parallel tasks no longer stall on a single gmem port (HLS 200-885 on gmem)
pair with hls::stream or proven stage overlap — distinct bundles alone do not fix decorative DATAFLOW
guards: each bundle still needs burst-friendly access patterns on its port
do not duplicate bundle names across unrelated ports
cosim and interface pragmas must stay consistent after rebundling
skills.template:
// BAD: all ports share one bundle — DATAFLOW tasks serialize on gmem
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=A bundle=gmem
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=B bundle=gmem
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=y bundle=gmem

// GOOD: one bundle per port for concurrent stage access
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=A bundle=gmem0
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=B bundle=gmem1
#pragma HLS INTERFACE m_axi port=y bundle=gmem2

guards: do not use DATAFLOW if stages are still sequentially dependent on the same buffer instance
do not create streams without bounded production/consumption behavior
avoid deadlock-prone stream cycles
skills.pattern: load, compute, and store logic is mixed in a single loop or function, preventing DATAFLOW scheduling or stage overlap
required_steps: extract load stage
extract compute stage
extract store stage
define buffer or stream interfaces between stages
ensure no hidden cross-stage dependence prevents overlap
apply DATAFLOW at parent scope
check dataflow report for actual concurrency
skills.strategy: split the code into explicit producer/consumer stages connected by local buffers or streams, then apply DATAFLOW at the parent scope when dependencies allow

guards: do not read from a buffer before it has been loaded
do not store a tile before it has been computed
do not drop the final tile during drain
skills.pattern: a double-buffered loop overlaps stages across tile indices and therefore requires prologue, steady-state, and epilogue handling
required_steps: extend loop bounds for startup/drain
guard load for t < NUM_TILES
guard compute for t > 0 and t <= NUM_TILES
guard store for t > 1 or equivalent
handle partial final tile
skills.strategy: guard load, compute, and store stages by tile index so the first and last overlapped iterations do not read uninitialized buffers or write invalid outputs

guards: do not add ping-pong buffers unless overlap is possible
avoid excessive local memory use
preserve first and last tile behavior
avoid read/write hazards between buffers
skills.pattern: the kernel processes data in chunks or tiles, and load, compute, and store phases for consecutive chunks currently execute serially
required_steps: identify chunk/tile loop
split load, compute, and store stages
create at least two local buffers per overlapped data stream
alternate buffers using tile index parity
handle prologue and epilogue iterations
apply DATAFLOW if stages have legal producer/consumer dependencies
validate functional correctness and actual phase overlap
skills.strategy: split the design into load, compute, and store stages; allocate ping-pong buffers; overlap load of tile k+1, compute of tile k, and optionally store of tile k-1

guards: do not duplicate very large buffers if memory usage exceeds budget
do not overlap stages that access the same buffer instance
validate schedule and correctness
skills.pattern: a tiled or chunked computation has one local buffer, causing the next load to wait for current compute or store to finish
required_steps: identify the buffer that causes serialization
allocate two buffers of the same shape
use t & 1 or equivalent parity for buffer selection
ensure producer and consumer use different buffers in the same overlapped iteration
handle startup and drain iterations
skills.strategy: duplicate the local buffer into ping-pong buffers and alternate producer/consumer stages across them

skills.pattern: kernel runs two passes over the same matrix with different access (row-major then transposed/column) and places tile for-loops inside #pragma HLS DATAFLOW that call load_* on the same m_axi port each iteration — HLS 200-1013
skills.strategy: Under DATAFLOW: one fused_load_task reads the matrix from m_axi once per element and fills both row-major and transposed local buffers in the same pipelined loop; load all vectors in the same or parallel tasks; run phase1_task and phase2_task on locals only; fused_store_task for outputs. No outer tile loop inside DATAFLOW that touches m_axi.
required_steps: replace per-tile load loops inside DATAFLOW with single fused_load_task covering full N×N (or legal tile stream pipeline with hls::stream, not repeated m_axi loads)
in fused load: for each (i,j) read A[i][j] once; write local_A_row[i][j] and local_A_col[j][i]
phase1_task uses local_A_row; phase2_task uses local_A_col — no m_axi in either
optional ARRAY_PARTITION on row locals for UNROLL in compute
verify no HLS 200-1013 on matrix port
guards: BRAM must fit both layouts — partition/unroll compute not load
pair with hls-single-load-dual-local-layout
distinct gmemN on vector ports enables parallel y1/y2 loads with fused A load
preserve first-tile and last-tile behavior
avoid double buffering if local memory usage becomes too high
do not introduce read/write hazards between ping-pong buffers
do not use DATAFLOW if function/loop dependencies prevent overlap
skills.pattern: the implementation uses tiles, but loading a tile and computing the tile execute serially across tile iterations and the schedule cannot overlap memory movement with computation
required_steps: split load_tile and compute_tile into separate functions or loops
allocate two local tile buffers
alternate buffers using tile index parity
guard first and last tile iterations
apply DATAFLOW only when there is a legal producer/consumer structure
validate correctness after overlapping phases
skills.strategy: use two local tile buffers in ping-pong fashion to overlap loading tile k+1 with computing tile k, and optionally storing tile k-1, using DATAFLOW only when producer/consumer structure is legal

guards: do not create cyclic streams without a proven schedule
producer and consumer token counts must match or be explicitly framed
DATAFLOW does not remove true data dependencies
stream depth tuning is required for variable-latency stages
skills.pattern: one stage in a loop body has variable or long latency, such as memory access, filtering, parsing, or conditional work, and it serializes otherwise independent producer/consumer work
required_steps: identify separable producer/compute/consumer work in the loop body
extract stages into functions or loops with clear interfaces
connect stages with hls::stream or bounded local FIFOs
set stream depth large enough to absorb burstiness but small enough for resources
apply DATAFLOW at the parent scope
guard stream counts so producer and consumer agree exactly
validate no deadlock and inspect dataflow viewer/report
skills.strategy: split the loop body into producer, compute, and consumer stages connected by hls::stream FIFOs under DATAFLOW, so backpressure is localized and independent stages can run concurrently

guards: do not stage unbounded arrays into local memory
DATAFLOW requires legal producer/consumer structure and bounded stream behavior
do not change host ABI or pointer types unless explicitly allowed
if each element is used once and access is already streaming, staging should still enable burst/dataflow or it may add overhead
skills.pattern: a pipelined compute loop directly issues m_axi/gmem reads and immediately consumes the response, or directly writes results, so request/response latency or AXI scheduling prevents low II
required_steps: identify m_axi reads/writes inside the II-limited compute loop
split global load, compute, and global store into separate loops or functions
make load/store addresses contiguous and burst-friendly where possible
stage bounded chunks into local buffers or streams
apply DATAFLOW at the parent scope when stages can run concurrently
use ping-pong buffers for tiled/chunked stages when the same buffer would serialize load and compute
set appropriate burst length and outstanding transaction pragmas where legal
pipeline compute over local memory and validate burst/report behavior
skills.strategy: decouple global-memory request/response from compute by splitting load, compute, and store stages; use burst-friendly load/store loops, local buffers or hls::stream FIFOs, DATAFLOW, and optionally ping-pong buffering to keep compute working on local data

guards: do not use old/new buffering for algorithms that intentionally require immediate in-place Gauss-Seidel-style updates
ensure swap/copy-back occurs at the correct time-step granularity
do not double buffer arrays so large that BRAM/URAM use becomes infeasible
preserve boundary cells and unchanged elements
skills.pattern: an iterative update reads old values and writes new values through the same array, causing loop-carried RAW/WAR hazards or forcing sequential update semantics when Jacobi-style old/new separation is valid
required_steps: determine whether the algorithm can use old/new state separation without changing semantics
allocate separate input/current and output/next local buffers
load the current state into the read buffer
rewrite the compute loop to read only from old/current and write only to new/next
swap buffer roles or copy back after each iteration/time step
partition the read buffer if multiple reads per cycle block II
pipeline the compute loop and validate boundary handling
skills.strategy: split storage into old and new buffers, compute from a read-only old buffer into a write-only new buffer, and swap or copy buffers between time steps; prefer full-grid or line-buffer old/new staging over spatial tiling with per-tile global load/store inside each iteration; combine with partitioning when multiple neighbor reads are needed per cycle

guards: do not add two buffers if phases still execute serially
do not use DATAFLOW when stage dependencies prevent overlap
avoid double buffering if local memory usage becomes excessive
preserve first-tile and last-tile behavior
skills.pattern: load, compute, and/or store phases operate on consecutive chunks or tiles but currently execute serially with no overlap
required_steps: split load, compute, and store into separable stages
allocate two or more local buffers for ping-pong scheduling
use tile index parity to alternate buffers
guard first and last iterations
apply DATAFLOW only when dependencies allow overlap
validate that phases overlap and local memory usage remains acceptable
skills.strategy: create ping-pong local buffers and a legal producer/consumer schedule so load of tile k+1 overlaps compute of tile k and optionally store of tile k-1
